evidence.R1-02: round0 G-04 line 27 is only a necessary condition ('repeats it only when ...') and cites only SG-01; it grants no permission, so CO-06 line 77 ('a second CO-A2 only after ... a lookup ... shows the order still placed or processing') and the CO-S12-S14 Forbidden lines decide a blind resend, with no conflict in the verdict.
evidence.R1-07: round0 failure row line 102 says without condition 'Make CO-A3 once more, relying on SG-01', which follows packet case 3 'agent retries once, then re-reads', so a run that skips the retry breaks a stated rule and every grader fails it; the 'exactly twice' count is not ambiguous.
evidence.R2-05: round1 never defines 'proposal'; Scope line 37 allows 'tell the customer which of their orders can be cancelled and what the refund would be', and rubric line 1464 'states no proposal for an order before the customer names one' leaves a which-order question that lists each order's refund open to opposite verdicts.
evidence.R2-07: round1 §5.1 line 1420 ends a trial only on an agent message or the 12-message cap, Appendix A line 1477 says 'The agent may repeat CO-A1 without limit', and CO-S10 line 621 'does not answer any CO-A1', so an agent that keeps retrying the lookup has no defined end of trial.
evidence.R2-08: round1 line 99 says 'propose the changed proposal' when the customer changes 'another proposal term' in the confirming turn, while line 98 and CO-03 line 68 allow only the total paid to the order's payment method and 'proposes nothing else'. A 'Yes, but to my Mastercard' turn matches both rows, and no scenario covers that case.
evidence.R3-05: round2 CO-S16 (lines 987-1002) covers packet case 3 (timeout, then a successful retry) but checks the message only with 'Refund id reported', and CO-S01 lists G-03 but uses only 'Refund id reported' and 'No arrival date promised' (line 1572/1583), so nothing checks the packet's 'Final message must match the final refund status' on these paths.
